classification.difficultyReason: Find a central angle using the cosine rule, then compare the corresponding arc length with its chord in a road context.

content.prompt: A straight road was constructed to cut a dangerous bend on a country road. It was found that the bend was part of an arc of radius $180\text{ m}$ and the straight road was $240\text{ m}$ long.

spec.description: Horizontal chord, dashed minor arc above it, and two dashed equal radii meeting below the chord. Matching radius ticks and the central angle label are retained. Ordinary source blue road strokes use house black; solid and dashed strokes preserve the road distinction.
spec.mathematics: Radius 180 m; chord 240 m; central angle theta. Diagram coordinates use radius 3 and chord 4, preserving the supplied ratio.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied lengths, equality ticks and theta are visible; no calculated angle or arc length is shown.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use cosine rule to find $\theta$ in radians, to 2 d.p.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the distance by which the old road was shortened, to the nearest metre.

answer.worked:
Use the unrounded angle from part a.
$$\begin{align*}l&=r\theta\\l&=180\cos^{-1}\left(\frac19\right)\text{ m}\\\text{Distance shortened}&=180\cos^{-1}\left(\frac19\right)-240\text{ m}\\\text{Distance shortened}&\approx23\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
